prompt: Which expression is equivalent to $3x^{-2}$, for $x \neq 0$?
hint: A negative exponent means reciprocal, not negative.

hints.text: A negative exponent means reciprocal, not negative.
The exponent $-2$ belongs to $x$ only, not to the coefficient $3$.

learningObjective: Rewrite a negative exponent as a reciprocal.
explanation: A negative exponent flips its base into the denominator: $x^{-2} = \dfrac{1}{x^2}$.
The coefficient $3$ has no negative exponent, so it stays in the numerator: $\dfrac{3}{x^2}$.
Choice A treats the negative exponent as a negative sign. Choice C wrongly moves the $3$ down with the $x$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Only what carries the exponent moves
steps: Had the expression been $(3x)^{-2}$, the whole product would move down, giving $\dfrac{1}{9x^2}$.
Reading exactly what the exponent attaches to is the whole question here — and it is a standard SAT distinction.
